es.term: HTAIE (hipertensión arterial inducida por el embarazo)
aliases: hipertensión arterial inducida por el embarazo
es.summary: Presión arterial alta que aparece después de las 20 semanas de embarazo. Incluye la hipertensión gestacional y la preeclampsia, que puede evolucionar a eclampsia o síndrome HELLP.
key_points: Se diagnostica con presión sistólica de 140 mm Hg o más, o diastólica de 90 mm Hg o más, en más de una toma.
Hipertensión gestacional: sin proteinuria ni daño de órganos; suele desaparecer en las 12 semanas tras el parto.
Preeclampsia: además hay proteinuria o signos de daño de órganos (hígado, riñón, cerebro).
Eclampsia: preeclampsia con convulsiones. HELLP: hemólisis, enzimas hepáticas altas y plaquetas bajas.
Si la hipertensión empezó antes de las 20 semanas, es hipertensión crónica (no HTAIE).

usage: Ejemplo: «G1P0, 34 semanas, HTAIE, PA 150/95, proteinuria negativa».
Algunos servicios usan HIE o «trastorno hipertensivo del embarazo»; la clasificación actual distingue HTA gestacional y preeclampsia.
nursing_care: Tomar la PA en posición sentada, con el brazo a la altura del corazón y el manguito adecuado.
Vigilar signos de alarma: cefalea intensa, visión borrosa, dolor en epigastrio, edema súbito y disminución de orina.
Vigilar el bienestar fetal: hay riesgo de RCI y DPP.
Administrar antihipertensivos y sulfato de magnesio según orden médica.

en.summary: High blood pressure that appears after 20 weeks of pregnancy (HTAIE in Spanish). It includes gestational hypertension and preeclampsia, which can progress to eclampsia or HELLP syndrome.
key_points: A formal diagnosis can be made when systolic blood pressure exceeds 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure exceeds 90 mm Hg on more than one occasion.
Gestational hypertension: no protein in the urine or organ damage; it usually goes away within 12 weeks after childbirth.
Preeclampsia also often includes signs of damage to some organs, such as the liver or kidneys, including protein in the urine.
Eclampsia: preeclampsia with seizures. HELLP: damage to the liver and blood cells.
Chronic hypertension is high blood pressure that starts before the 20th week of pregnancy (not PIH).

usage: Example: "G1P0, 34 weeks, PIH, BP 150/95, urine protein negative".
Some units use HIE or "hypertensive disorder of pregnancy"; current classification separates gestational hypertension and preeclampsia.
nursing_care: Take BP seated, with the arm at heart level and the right cuff size.
Watch for warning signs: severe headache, blurred vision, epigastric pain, sudden swelling and decreased urine output.
Monitor fetal well-being: there is a risk of growth restriction and placental abruption.
Give antihypertensives and magnesium sulfate as ordered.

summary.1.quote: Magnesium Sulfate Indication: treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, such as gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and eclampsia, that develop during pregnancy

key_points.0.quote: A formal diagnosis can be made when systolic blood pressure exceeds 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure exceeds 90 mm Hg on more than one occasion.

key_points.2.quote: Preeclampsia also often includes signs of damage to some of your organs, such as your liver or kidneys.

key_points.3.quote: When a person with preeclampsia or eclampsia has damage to the liver and blood cells, it's called HELLP syndrome .

key_points.4.quote: Chronic hypertension is high blood pressure that starts before the 20th week of pregnancy or before you became pregnant.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Patients often experience signs and symptoms of preeclampsia, such as epigastric pain, headache, and vision changes, but the patient may not necessarily develop hypertension or proteinuria (Alese et al., 2021).
